It reprocessed old mine waste near Baia Mare to recover gold and silver using a cyanide carbon-in-pulp process, designed for 2.5 million tonnes a year and about 1.6 tonnes of gold and 9.0 tonnes of silver annually, and began operating in May 1999.

B2Gold.desc: A Canadian gold mining company headquartered in Vancouver and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (BTO), NYSE American (BTG) and the Namibian Stock Exchange (B2G). It operates the Fekola mine in Mali (80% owned), Masbate in the Philippines and Otjikoto in Namibia (90%), and reported total gold production of 804,778 ounces in 2024.

BASF.desc: A chemical company organised in six segments: Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, Nutrition & Care, Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. Sales were EUR 65.3 billion in 2024, with 111,822 employees at year-end.

BBVA Previsión AFP and Futuro de Bolivia.desc: The two private pension fund administrators (AFPs) licensed in Bolivia after an international tender awarded in January 1997. BBVA holds about 80% of BBVA Prevision AFP, which was set up in Bolivia in February 1997 and licensed that April for the country's southeast; Futuro de Bolivia S.A. AFP was created by the Invesco-Argentaria consortium for the northwest, with Argentaria as majority shareholder, and BBVA sold its stake in Futuro in March 2001.

BOTAŞ.desc: Turkey's state-owned oil and gas pipeline company (Boru Hatlari ile Petrol Tasima A.S.), a state enterprise with joint-stock company status whose capital belongs to the Turkish treasury, set up on 15 August 1974 to carry Iraqi crude oil to Iskenderun Bay. It transports crude oil and handles the transport, distribution, import, storage, trade and export of natural gas, including LNG reception and gas storage.

BP Exploration Company (Colombia).desc: BP's oil and gas exploration, production and transportation business in Colombia, holding interests in five producing fields (including Cusiana, Pauto and Florena), a stake in the Cusiana gas processing plant, interests in four pipelines and 24.8% of the OCENSA crude oil pipeline, with net production of about 25,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day. In 2010 Ecopetrol (51%) and Canada's Talisman (49%) agreed to buy 100% of its shares for $1.9 billion.

BSES (Bombay Suburban Electric Supply).desc: An Indian electricity company that supplied power over its own network, chaired by Anil Ambani. It no longer uses that name: shareholders voted on 10 June 2003 to rename it Reliance Energy Ltd, alongside plans for transmission and electricity trading subsidiaries.

BTC Co (BP-led consortium).desc: A separately incorporated company formed in August 2002 to build and run the 1,768 km Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan oil pipeline from Azerbaijan through Georgia and Turkey to the Ceyhan Marine Terminal, with capacity of one million barrels of oil a day. Its shareholders are BP (30.1%), AzBTC (25.00%), MOL (8.90%), Equinor (8.71%), TPAO (6.53%), Eni (5.00%), Total (5.00%), ITOCHU (3.40%), INPEX (2.50%), ExxonMobil (2.50%) and ONGC (BTC) Limited (2.36%).

Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.desc: An Indian state-owned special purpose vehicle, a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Karnataka, which builds and operates the Bengaluru Metro Rail project (Namma Metro). Its operating network is 96.10 km across three corridors.

Bangladesh Water Development Board.desc: The Bangladeshi government's main water management agency, under the Ministry of Water Resources and governed by the BWDB Act 2000. It began in 1959 as the water wing of the East Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority and was reconstituted as a separate autonomous body in 1972; it builds and maintains flood control, drainage and irrigation works, and had built 10,224 km of embankments as of the 2008-09 financial year.

Bangladesh-China Power Company (BCPCL).desc: A Bangladeshi joint venture company incorporated on 1 October 2014 to build and run power projects, chiefly the 1,320 MW Payra thermal power plant at Dhankhali, Kalapara, in Patuakhali district. It is owned 50-50 by North-West Power Generation Company Limited, a Bangladeshi state-owned company, and China National Machinery Import & Export Corporation, a wholly state-owned Chinese company.
